sentences.text: Rhizodus belonged to the Rhizodontida, one of the earliest-diverging tetrapodomorph clades.
The genus is classified within the class Sarcopterygii.
The type species measured between 5.14 and 5.63 meters long and weighed between 1 and 1.5 metric tons.
Rhizodus was scientifically described by Owen in 1840.
The type species Rhizodus hibberti was discovered in the Viséan stage of the United Kingdom.
The species Rhizodus serpukhovensis was discovered in the Serpukhovian of Russia.
Fossils of Rhizodus have also been found in North America.
A partial lower jaw found in Russia was formally described as the new species R. serpukhovensis in 2022.
Both valid species of Rhizodus lived during the Early Carboniferous epoch.
Rhizodus lived from the Tournaisian to the Gzhelian, between 358.86 and 298.9 million years ago.
A 2020 study suggested dividing rhizodont humeri into four morphogroups to better identify Rhizodus.
